invariants.rule: bleeding, perfusion, compression, tissue damage, repair integrity, and success are derived from post-physics scene observations rather than policy action fields
clinical effects use the configured jaw-to-substrate force matrix and never substitute an unfiltered net-force sensor
single-pad force, asymmetric squeezing, closure away from the authored target neighborhood, or motion without target contact cannot produce useful compression
temporary compression decays after physical contact release; retained repairs and ventilation remain effective only while current-interval attachment and scene evidence continues
excessive or unstable force accumulates vessel or tissue damage and cannot improve the patient outcome

reward is based on measured flow improvement, blood loss, distal perfusion, shared patient MAP and oxygenation change, new damage, and one-time verification transitions; favorable-state dwell earns no reward
hemostasis verification requires a continuous measured upstream-pressure challenge across physics frames; a policy request cannot activate the challenge or set its result
the system never represents simulation thresholds as patient-care settings
